author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nurses at Boston Medical Center have voted to authorize a three-day strike as contract negotiations continue over wages and staffing. Nearly 90% of participating nurses supported the authorization, according to their union, 1199SEIU. The bargaining unit covers almost 2,000 nurses at the hospital’s Boston campus and Brockton Behavioral Health Center.

The vote does not automatically trigger a walkout. Union leaders would still have to set dates and provide the required 10-day notice before a strike could begin. Nurses and the hospital have been negotiating for more than six months. The union says compensation remains well below competing systems and argues that vacancies and turnover place additional pressure on bedside staff.

Boston Medical Center has said its proposal would raise pay by 15% to 20% over two years, depending on seniority, and has pointed to financial constraints facing the safety-net system. The union says a substantial gap remains between the sides. The authorization gives negotiators leverage for the next round of talks while leaving time for an agreement that would avoid disruption for patients and employees.
dek: Nearly 90% of voting nurses backed strike authority as contract talks remain divided over pay and staffing, though no walkout has been scheduled.
headline: Boston Medical Center nurses authorize three-day strike
